title: Moffat Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Moffat wells have a 209-foot median depth, 15 gpm median yield, and estimated finished costs of $16,400-$27,700.
h1: Moffat, Colorado Well Depth, Water and Drilling Costs
intro_html:
This page covers permitted wells within 5 miles of Moffat in Saguache County. The records show a wide range of drilling conditions, from shallow wells in alluvial ground to much deeper wells associated with fractured bedrock. Of 466 wells in Colorado DWR permit records, 339 are recorded as constructed. Depth is reported for 290 wells, pump yield for 40, and static water level for 30.

For a buyer, the useful starting point is the local pattern: the median well is 209 feet deep, the median reported yield is 15 gpm, and the median static water level is 6 feet below ground. Those figures help with early planning, but they do not replace a site-specific well and water-rights review.

sections.heading: How deep are wells around Moffat?
sections.html:
Moffat wells have a median reported depth of 209 feet. The middle half runs from 111 to 430 feet, so a driller bidding a new well here should account for a broad range rather than treating 209 feet as a guaranteed target. The 90th percentile is 792 feet, and the deepest well in the records reaches 1,980 feet.

Depth is split across several ranges: 18% are under 100 feet, 38% are between 100 and 300 feet, 30% are between 300 and 600 feet, and 15% are deeper than 600 feet. Permits name unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifers for 250 wells, alongside the Confined San Luis Valley aquifer and Unconfined San Luis Vall aquifer. Those formations help explain why nearby lots can require very different drilling depths.

sections.heading: What water yield can you expect near Moffat?
sections.html:
The reported median pump yield is 15 gpm, with the middle half between 12.0 and 17.5 gpm. Seventy percent of the reported wells produce more than 15 gpm, while 28% fall between 5 and 15 gpm. Only 2% are in the 1-to-5-gpm range, and none of the reported wells are under 1 gpm.

That is a favorable local record, but the yield data cover only 40 wells, not all 466 permits. A strong yield also does not establish drinking-water quality or legal availability for every use. Ask for the well construction report, pump information, and any production testing before relying on a neighboring well as a promise for your lot. Household wells remain subject to their permit conditions and applicable Colorado water rules.

sections.heading: What does the water table show in Moffat?
sections.html:
Reported static water levels are shallow in this area. The median depth to water is 6 feet below the surface, with the middle half from 0 to 11 feet. Only 30 wells report a static water level, so these figures are a useful local indication rather than a complete groundwater survey.

The decade comparison does not suggest a dropping water table in the available records. The median measurement was 11 feet below surface in the 2010s and 6 feet in the 2020s, meaning the later reported measurements were closer to the surface. That difference can reflect location, season, well construction, and the small reporting set. A buyer should still have the actual well measured and reviewed, especially where shallow water may affect excavation, septic design, or basement planning.

sections.heading: Who has drilled near Moffat, and when?
sections.html:
Permit history around Moffat extends across several generations. The records show 12 permits from the 1950s, 19 from the 1960s, 76 from the 1970s, 22 from the 1980s, 77 from the 1990s, 59 from the 2000s, 69 from the 2010s, and 40 from the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2025, so this is not an area with only old well information.

The most active drillers named in these records are Valley Pump Company (Self, Clinton L.) with 30 wells, Heersink Drilling (Heersink, Scott) with 16, and A. E. Biggs & Son (Biggs, A E) with 15. That history can help identify contractors familiar with local formations, but permit counts are not endorsements. Confirm current licensing, insurance, references, and the proposed casing, grout, testing, and pump scope.

sections.heading: What does a new well cost near Moffat?
sections.html:
The local cost model uses mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground and a drilling rate of $50 to $75 per foot. At the 209-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to about $10,400 to $15,700. That is the drilling portion, not the complete water system.

A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $16,400 to $27,700 at the median depth. The wide depth distribution matters: a 111-foot well and a 430-foot well can produce very different bids even before site access, casing, grout, surface completion, or difficult drilling are considered. Request a written estimate that states the assumed depth, what happens if the hole is dry or low-yielding, and which equipment and connections are included.

sections.heading: What risks should Moffat buyers investigate?
sections.html:
Low yield is not the main pattern in the reported data, but a small reporting set cannot eliminate the risk of a poor well or a dry hole on a particular parcel. Fractured-bedrock wells are especially variable because productive water may depend on intersecting the right fractures. The aquifer name on a permit is not a guarantee of either quantity or quality.

Environmental records within about 10 miles include 2 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 6 historic mine features, and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. That does not prove a problem on a specific property, but it supports testing the existing well for routine drinking-water concerns and any site-specific contaminants. Check septic setbacks, well location, groundwater depth, access for a rig, and whether the lot can support the planned building and wastewater system.

sections.heading: Buying or building on a Moffat lot
sections.html:
Before closing, obtain the Colorado DWR permit and construction report, verify the well location, and compare the well's actual depth, pump, yield, and static level with nearby records. Pay particular attention to the middle-half depth range of 111 to 430 feet rather than budgeting only from the 209-foot median. A neighboring well is useful evidence, not a guarantee.

For a new build, have the driller and septic designer review access, drilling clearance, casing and grout, trench routes, electrical service, and wastewater setbacks together. Domestic and household use account for 48% of the listed use mix, while stock accounts for 52% and irrigation appears on 22% of permits. Confirm the permit allows the intended use. If the property is in an over-appropriated basin, ask a water-rights professional whether an augmentation plan is needed.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Moffat, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth near Moffat is 209 feet. The middle half of reported depths runs from 111 to 430 feet. Some wells are much deeper: the 90th percentile is 792 feet, and the deepest record is 1,980 feet. A local driller should price the parcel based on nearby construction reports, not the median alone.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Moffat?
faq.a: The drilling model for Moffat uses $50 to $75 per foot in mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground. At the 209-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $10,400 to $15,700. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $16,400 to $27,700. Actual bids depend heavily on depth and site conditions.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Moffat?
faq.a: The median reported pump yield is 15 gpm, with the middle half between 12.0 and 17.5 gpm. Seventy percent of reported wells produce more than 15 gpm. However, only 40 wells report a pump yield, so those results are not a guarantee for an untested parcel. Review the construction report and obtain site-specific testing before planning water use.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Moffat?
faq.a: The well records describe depth and production, not drinking-water safety. Within about 10 miles, mapped environmental records include 2 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 6 historic mine features, and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site. Test an existing or new well through a qualified laboratory, and ask for additional testing based on the property's location and history.

faq.q: Is the water table dropping near Moffat?
faq.a: The available records do not show a dropping trend. Median static water level was 11 feet below the surface in the 2010s and 6 feet in the 2020s, so later reported measurements were shallower. Only 30 wells report static water levels, and differences may reflect location, season, or construction. Measure the specific well rather than relying only on the area summary.
